A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoRA research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching content relocated between versions.

before.justification: v4 reports original downstream prediction results, baseline comparisons, scaling experiments, ablations, sensitivity studies and distillation results.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds an urban carbon-emissions prediction experiment in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The core encoders, contrastive objectives and distillation procedure remain unchanged. v5 Appendix A.2 adds a limited application-specific adaptation by augmenting static 128-dimensional representations with cyclical time-of-year and time-of-day features for carbon-emissions prediction.

E1.justification: v5 adds nationwide urban carbon-emissions prediction for 2020–2024 using a satellite-derived dataset, extending evaluation into an environmental task with temporal variation. The existing nine socio-economic tasks and geographic coverage remain unchanged. The new dataset's citation is unresolved.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the national comparison, Jiangsu comparison and distillation experiment. The added carbon-emissions evaluation reuses AlphaEarth, an existing comparator; no comparison method is added to or removed from a retained experiment.

E3.justification: The new carbon-emissions experiment introduces temporal feature augmentation into downstream evaluation. Existing training settings, downstream evaluation procedures and resolution-study protocols are retained. The carbon experiment does not specify its evaluation split or sample count.

E4.justification: The anchoring, module, neighborhood-graph, sampling, auxiliary-modality and H3-resolution analyses are unchanged. v4 Appendices A.5–A.6 move into v5 Section 4.4 with matching procedures and results. The carbon experiment adds task coverage rather than an ablation or controlled robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten-run reporting statement and identical standard deviations in Table 2. v5 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed information or significance test; the carbon results are reported without accompanying uncertainty.

E6.justification: v5 Appendix A.2 newly reports carbon-emissions R² values of 0.612 for MoRA and 0.605 for AlphaEarth. All matched existing numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. These are additional task results, not a demonstrated performance improvement from v4 to v5 under retained settings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the mathematical model specification and distillation objective remain unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs beyond the retained material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: mobility-backed multimodal representations, the nine-task benchmark, the claimed 12.9% average improvement, scaling behavior and coordinate-based distilled inference. The carbon application is discussed outside these core contribution statements.

C2.justification: v5 Section 4.2 and Appendix A.2 interpret the carbon result as evidence that mobility captures human activity driving environmental externalities that physical encoders may overlook. The ethics statement newly specifies that aggregation records no precise coordinates. Existing scale and mobility-data availability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 generalizes the WeChat Pay attribution to Tencent and omits v4's explicit same-user weekly linkage rule and undirected, weighted edge description. The WorldPop 2018 reference and resource link disappear. Training and distillation details and code-access statements elsewhere remain, so these are documentation changes without evidence of changed underlying graph construction.

R1.justification: The WorldPop 2018 reference is removed, while the related-work discussion and principal positioning against earlier representation-learning approaches remain unchanged. WorldPop citations in Section 4.1.1 and Table 1 become unresolved; the Bondarenko et al. reference remains elsewhere.

P1.justification: v5 integrates two existing appendix studies into Section 4.4, reorders the remaining appendices, adds acknowledgements and author emails, and revises several passages. It also fixes the unresolved modality-ablation table cross-reference. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: All four figure images are identical. Figure 2 is repositioned, and v4 Tables 6–7 move into the main text as v5 Tables 4–5; distillation and scaling tables are renumbered and repositioned. Some captions explicitly add R², and the author block becomes more compact.

improvement.justification: v5 makes existing ablation evidence easier to find and adds an environmental application. However, the carbon comparison has an unresolved dataset citation and lacks an explicit evaluation split, sample count and uncertainty, limiting the evidential value of its 0.007 R² margin. Reduced graph-construction specificity and broken WorldPop citations also weaken documentation. These benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
